title: CAR-005 Route Policy Fixture
description: The declared routing policy for one synthetic agent: a preferred route, an ordered list of fallback routes, the three declared budgets, and optionally the policy's own declared optional helper. This document is deliberately PERMISSIVE about the defects the simulator exists to diagnose (FR-003a): a route's resolved_model and effort stay optional and fallback_routes declares no uniqueItems, because a schema strict enough to reject an inherit-materialization route or a revisited fallback would make those fixtures fail validation instead of producing the diagnostic the requirement asks for. The declared budget maxima are the deliberate inverse (FR-027): an out-of-range budget is simply invalid input and is rejected here rather than surfacing as a diagnostic. No $ref leaves this document's own #/$defs/ (FR-016).

preferred_route.description: FR-004: the route resolution attempts first.

fallback_routes.description: FR-004: attempted in declared order after the preferred route. minItems 0 admits the edge case of an empty fallback list whose preferred rejection leads directly to no_safe_route. uniqueItems is deliberately NOT declared: FR-020 requires a fixture whose chain revisits an already-attempted route, and uniqueItems would make that fixture unrepresentable, converting a required diagnostic into a validation error (FR-003a).

optional_helper.description: FR-025b: optional. Its absence is FR-025a's third helper state — the policy declares no helper at all — which is why the member is not required.

agentIdentity.description: FR-018: the reported subject. Names are synthetic and fixture- prefixed; no shipped agent name appears in any fixture, with the roster read live from speckit-pro/agents/ rather than transcribed here.

role_class.description: The three classes the spec's assumptions fix. Each is the subject or declared helper of at least one corpus case (FR-018).

route.description: One declared candidate route. route_id is the attempt-order identity a fallback_loop revisit is recognised by (FR-020).

alias.description: FR-003: the pinned alias. FR-006 reads it against the snapshot's alias_bindings table.

resolved_model.description: FR-003a: the pinned qualified resolved model ID, deliberately OPTIONAL. FR-023 requires a route omitting it to be rejected at resolution with silent_inherit_materialization; requiring it here would fail that fixture at validation and no diagnostic would ever be produced.

effort.description: FR-007a: the closed five-member Claude ladder, in order, reusing the frozen ordered ladder successor-capability-freeze.schema.json already pins so this feature introduces no parallel effort vocabulary. Scope is the subagent-frontmatter surface; ultracode is deliberately not a member, being a session-level orchestration setting rather than a model effort level. Deliberately OPTIONAL for the same FR-023 reason as resolved_model (FR-003a).

qualified.description: Fixture-declared qualification, per the spec's assumption that qualification is an input rather than something this simulation derives.

adjacent_to.description: FR-021: a sibling route_id, encoding the adjacency relation the unqualified_adjacent_model violation is decided against.

substituted_agent.description: FR-022: present only when the route dispatches a different agent than the policy's subject. A generic class is what generic_agent_substitution is decided against.

declaredBudgets.description: FR-003 and FR-027: the three declared caps, each carrying both bounds so the maxima sit in the same object literal as the field's type — this directory's universal habit. Recorded caveat: bounding a max_* field from ABOVE with maximum has no exact precedent here (the existing budget precedent bounds such fields from below, because there the field's value IS the ceiling), so the keyword choice is this feature's own decision even though its placement follows convention. A declared 1 satisfies FR-028's budget-of-one exhaustion case; a declared 9 fails validation rather than being clamped at run time.

max_retries.description: FR-026a: minimum 0 where both sibling caps carry minimum 1, because 'no re-attempt' is coherent while 'never probe' is not. max_retries 1 therefore admits two consultations of one route.

declaredOptionalHelper.description: FR-025b: the member by which a policy declares its optional helper, so the helper the report describes is one the policy actually declares. It gives optional_helper.probe_attempts a domain to count over, distinguishes the three FR-025a helper states, and makes 'no helper route appears as attempted' falsifiable. No second budget set: the declared budgets stay on the policy root and the helper's accounting is the disjoint optional_helper.probe_attempts counter in the report.

agent.description: The helper's own identity. role_class is narrowed to optional_helper, which is what stops a required agent being declared in the helper slot.
